objections.claim: The branch publisher does not make agent-authored workflow changes inert. Publishing an agent-controlled branch can immediately trigger a newly added or modified `.github/workflows/*` workflow from that branch, giving the agent-controlled code a GitHub Actions token and potentially repository secrets before the merge controller evaluates the PR. That code can mutate repository state or attempt an out-of-band merge; post-attempt detection cannot restore fail-closed behavior. Protecting only verifier-invoking workflow digests and asserting that the agent process itself lacks credentials does not close this path. The approach must quarantine or reject agent-authored workflow changes before publication, or publish them through an execution-disabled/unprivileged fork boundary, and must prove with a regression that a malicious push/PR workflow cannot obtain mutation authority or secrets.
